validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real, dated, on-point independent source found -- Business Standard, 9 Jan 2019, 'H-Energy plans Rs 3,700 cr investment for LNG project in West Bengal' (business-standard.com, verified live, content confirmed via curl+grep since WebFetch on this domain 403s). It reports H-Energy's Rs 3,700 crore (~$556M) West Bengal regasification project: Rs 1,500 cr for a 3 MTPA FSRU terminal, Rs 2,200 cr for pipeline works. Critically, it states: 'The project dates back to August 2015 when H-Energy won a tender issued by the Kolkata Port Trust for commission and operation of a Floating Storage and Regasification Unit (FSRU). This FSRU will be located 115 km into the sea within the Kolkata Port Trust boundary limits and will be connected to the Onshore Receiving Facilities at Contai through a 115 km long subsea pipeline.' That sentence independently corroborates the sheet's Length (115 km), the EndLocation (Contai), the general geometry (subsea), and the owner (H-Energy). This is a real once-proposed project, not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity.

CITATION-ACCURACY FINDING (the sheet's own second citation is a mismatch): the row's current_ref for Status/Fuel/PipelineType also cites https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/economy/india-looks-to-export-rlng-to-bd-via-pipeline (11 Jun 2024). Fetched and checked in full: this article contains ZERO occurrences of 'Contai' and ZERO occurrences of '115'. It is about a DIFFERENT, later H-Energy pipeline project: 'H-Energy plans to supply the gas from Digha in West Bengal to Khulna in Bangladesh. This will require constructing a 155 km cross-border pipeline stretching from Kanai Chatta in East Medinipur district to Shrirampur in Khulna... 90 km laid within India and 65 km within Bangladesh.' That is the Kanai Chatta-Shrirampur corridor (cf. roster row P2214, and P6562 Kanai Chhata-Panitar noted elsewhere as a live construction row), not the Digha-Contai line. The existing_ref_checks in the worklist already flagged this FE URL as failing the 'cancelled' content screen for Status -- correctly, since the article never discusses this pipeline's status (or existence) at all. The FE citation should not be attached to this row's Status/Fuel/PipelineType cells.

NAMING PRECISION: neither citation states 'Digha' and 'Contai' together in one sentence for THIS pipeline. Business Standard names Contai as the onshore receiving facility but describes the offshore FSRU location only as '115 km into the sea within the Kolkata Port Trust boundary limits' -- it never calls that point 'Digha'. The only literal 'Digha' string in the BS article is attached to the OTHER (Khulna-bound) pipeline sentence. GEM's own wiki page synthesizes the 'Digha' name from the wider association of this H-Energy Kolkata-Port-Trust FSRU project with the Digha coastal area (consistent with FE's 2024 usage, which does call the source point 'Digha'), but strictly, the specific 115 km/Contai subsea line's start point is not independently pinned to the literal name 'Digha' in either citation. This is a soft caveat, not an existence problem -- the physical project (FSRU off the Bengal coast, 115 km subsea line to an onshore facility at Contai, H-Energy, ~3,700 cr, Jan 2019) is real and specific; only the precise 'Digha' label for the offshore end lacks a literal quote.

CORROBORATION TIER: only ONE genuinely on-point independent source was found for this specific route/length/owner (Business Standard 2019) -- the second cited source (FE) does not corroborate it, so this row does not clear the 2-independent-source bar and should be treated as medium tier, not high, for its substantive facts. Extensive further search for a second corroborating source or a formal cancellation notice was attempted (WebSearch quota was already exhausted this session before this row was reached; DuckDuckGo, Bing, Ecosia and Startpage all returned bot-challenge pages to direct curl fetches, and h-energy.com is a JS-only SPA with no server-rendered content) and came up empty -- reported here as an honest search limitation rather than a settled 'no second source exists'.

CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both reasonable/uncontested -- a dedicated large-diameter subsea line moving regasified LNG from an FSRU to shore is transmission-class infrastructure, not gathering/distribution, and this is inferable from context even though neither citation uses the word 'transmission' literally.

DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 13-row roster: no other row shares this exact Digha/Kolkata-Port-Trust-FSRU-to-Contai geometry. The nearest relative is P2214 Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur (also West Bengal, also traceable via the 2024 FE article to the same H-Energy Digha-sourced gas), but Kanai Chatta and Contai are different, non-adjacent onshore points in the same general district, and the two projects differ in era (2015-2019 domestic-distribution concept vs. a 2024-reported cross-border export concept) and length (115 km subsea vs. 155 km, 90 km of it in India). Not confident enough to call this a same-pipe duplicate outright -- flagging for the redundancy-adjudication step rather than merging here.

SPEC: Length=115 km matches the Business Standard figure exactly (independently, twice in the same sentence: FSRU '115 km into the sea' and 'a 115 km long subsea pipeline'). No material spec disagreement found.

fills.researcher_notes: Article states the FSRU-to-Contai subsea line is '115 km long' (and separately that the FSRU sits '115 km into the sea'), matching LengthKnown=115.00 km exactly. Only one on-point independent source found (see validity notes) -- medium tier, not high.

Article: 'H-Energy has lined up an investment of Rs 3,700 crore to set up a 3-million tonne (mt) regasification plant and a pipeline in West Bengal...' and quotes H-Energy's own MD/CEO Darshan Hiranandani -- H-Energy as sole sponsor/owner is directly stated. Same single-source caveat as Length.

Left UNRESOLVED rather than forced. EndLocation=Contai is directly stated by Business Standard ('Onshore Receiving Facilities at Contai'), but StartLocation=Digha is not stated by either citation for THIS specific 115 km line -- BS's only literal 'Digha' reference is attached to a different (Khulna-bound) pipeline sentence, and describes the FSRU location here only as '115 km into the sea within the Kolkata Port Trust boundary limits'. Filling the cluster would require splicing two half-supported facts into one claim; declining to do that per the no-fabrication standing rule. See validity notes for the full reasoning.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No formal cancellation/withdrawal source was found for this specific pipeline -- GEM's own wiki text itself says the project is 'now presumed cancelled' (its editors' inference, not a cited cancellation event). Last substantive news about THIS route (Digha-area FSRU to Contai onshore facility, 115 km subsea) is the Jan 2019 Business Standard announcement; nothing about Contai or this specific line surfaces afterward. Under the country's dormancy rule (proposed, no progress >=2y -> shelved; >=4y -> cancelled), 7+ years of silence on this specific route clears the cancelled threshold comfortably, so the recorded Status=cancelled is confirmed as the right call, but as an INFERRED dormancy conclusion, not a confirmed cancellation -- staging ShelvedCancelledType=inferred (currently blank) with no fabricated ref, per standing rule 2 and the annual-update instructions. Note a real complication for the country-level FSRU project as a whole (not this specific route): a June 2024 Financial Express article shows H-Energy still actively pursuing a Digha-sourced gas EXPORT deal with Bangladesh's Petrobangla via a different, newer pipeline (155 km Kanai Chatta-Shrirampur, matching/near the roster's P2214) -- so the broader H-Energy Digha LNG/FSRU concept was not entirely dead as of mid-2024, it appears to have pivoted away from the original Contai-bound domestic design captured here. That 2024 evidence supports a status conclusion about the FSRU project's newer incarnation, not about this specific Digha-Contai/115 km/Contai proposal, which is why it is not used as this row's evidence_date. Flagged for the redundancy-adjudication step (P3334 vs P2214) rather than treated as reviving this row.

summary: P3334 (Digha-Contai Gas Pipeline) is a real, once-proposed H-Energy subsea line (115 km, FSRU to an onshore receiving facility at Contai, West Bengal) confirmed by a single independent 2019 Business Standard source -- confirmed (caveat), not existence-hallucinated, but only medium-tier (the sheet's second citation, a 2024 Financial Express article, does not mention this pipeline at all and describes a different H-Energy Digha->Khulna line instead, so it should be dropped from this row).
